model_annotation: Figure 4 is a horizontal bar chart illustrating the frequency of perception among respondents regarding the most important measures they believe could help enterprises curb the "shadow economy" in the country. The horizontal axis represents the categorical labels for each proposed measure, listed in a specific order from top to bottom: "To strengthen border control," "To restrict mafia activities," "To improve credit conditions," "To reduce corruption," "To improve administrative efficiency," "To strengthen tax control," "To introduce more effective business incentives," "To adopt stricter laws," "To reduce tariffs," "To reduce VAT," "To reduce personal income tax." The vertical axis represents the percentage frequency of respondents' perception, with numerical values ranging from 0 to 15 percent, marked at intervals of 5 percent. The bars extend horizontally to indicate the percentage frequency associated with each measure; for instance, the measure "To reduce corruption" has the highest frequency at 13 percent, while "To strengthen border control" and "To reduce tariffs" both have the lowest frequency at 2 percent. The chart uses two distinct colors to differentiate between measures: blue bars are used for "To strengthen border control," "To improve credit conditions," "To strengthen tax control," "To adopt stricter laws," "To reduce tariffs," "To reduce VAT," and "To reduce personal income tax," while red bars are used for "To restrict mafia activities," "To reduce corruption," "To improve administrative efficiency," and "To introduce more effective business incentives." The bars are arranged in descending order of frequency from top to bottom. There is no visible legend or additional annotation indicating specific grouping or stacking of bars; each bar represents a single measure independently.
